analysis.title: Monthly Market Monitor (short version), November 2026
key_insights: Robeco remains long equities but cut emerging market exposure because South Korea and Taiwan face semiconductor pressure. It keeps developed market equity exposure on supportive growth, earnings and improving seasonality.
October saw a sharp tech-led sell-off in emerging markets. Global equities held broadly steady in euro terms.
Credit underweight is maintained because tight spreads offer limited upside. Borrowing to fund AI build-outs adds supply and financing risks.
Robeco switched high yield hedging from the US to Europe, where it sees debt markets as more vulnerable.
Robeco added US dollars, funded by selling euros, as rate differentials compressed. European growth headwinds and French political and debt risks support a cautious euro view.
Bonds recovered in October despite sticky inflation. Government bonds and credit gained while high yield edged lower.
Robeco prefers short-dated German and UK bonds, keeps a short in US Treasuries and stays underweight credit.

Oil surged on supply concerns while gold fell and real estate rebounded as yields shifted. Robeco stays cautious on oil because uncertainty over reopening the Strait of Hormuz makes the outlook hard to predict.
Theme of the month: Robeco expects the Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections to broaden US equity leadership beyond AI, with greater return dispersion that favors stock pickers.

Strong corporate earnings anchor the equity view. Earnings growth has outpaced price gains, easing valuations. Rising bond market volatility could spill into stocks, so earnings and interest rates are the key factors to watch.
The strategic AI investment thesis remains intact despite fears of a slower data center build-out. Investors want evidence that capex will generate sustainable cash flows and returns.
